title: UpDown: Combining Scalable Address Translation with Locality Control
problem: Traditional page-based address translation has limited reach for petabyte-scale distributed memory, while scalable segment-based techniques fail to provide effective data locality control.
motivation: Global shared memories of petabytes are increasingly useful for applications, requiring techniques that balance both scalable reach and fine-grained locality management.
method: UpDown proposes a two-level translation scheme that separates access control from data layout. The scheme provides compact, efficient access control to distributed segments of arbitrary size while enabling data layout control at the upper level. This decoupling allows applications to manage locality through user-level operations without requiring privileged operations.
key_novelty: Two-level address translation architecture that decouples access control from data layout, enabling scalable reach while maintaining fine-grained locality control.
contributions: Two-level translation scheme combining scalable address translation with locality control
Reduction of translation state by approximately 620 billion times total and 130 billion times for local state
User-level data locality management without privileged operations
Demonstration of scalability for petabyte-scale distributed memory systems

metrics.other: Translation state reduction: ~620B× total, ~130B× local state

limitations: Evaluation is limited to simulations with synthetic traces rather than real hardware implementation.
primary_theme: Scalable address translation with locality control
